name: Ranighat Durbar (Rani Mahal)
image_query: Rani Mahal Ranighat palace Kali Gandaki
tagline: Rana palace of 1893 on the Kali Gandaki, called Nepal's Taj Mahal
meta_description: Ranighat Durbar (Rani Mahal), Palpa: the 1893 Rana palace on the Kali Gandaki below Tansen. History, museum, walking trail, jeep road, timings and tips.
summary: Ranighat Durbar, better known as Rani Mahal, is a white neoclassical palace built in 1893 by General Khadga Shumsher Rana in memory of his wife Tej Kumari, on a rock above the Kali Gandaki about 13 km by road from Tansen. Restored in 2017 with a small museum, it makes a half-day trip from Tansen.
intro: Rani Mahal stands on a rocky spur above the Kali Gandaki, deep in a valley below the Tansen ridge. General Khadga Shumsher Rana, then posted to Palpa, had it built after the death of his youngest wife, Tej Kumari Devi, in 1892. The design, said to be by a British architect, mixes European neoclassical columns and arches with a Nepali setting of forest and river, and the memorial purpose earned it the nickname of Nepal's Taj Mahal. Khadga Shumsher fled to India in 1902 after falling out with the ruling branch of his family, and the palace was abandoned for most of a century.

After decades of decay, the Department of Archaeology carried out repairs, and in 2017 the government completed a fuller restoration and opened a museum inside. A road was also built along the Brangdi river to bring visitors closer. The white façade and river terraces are the main sights; the interior rooms are modest but give a sense of how Rana nobility lived away from Kathmandu.

Getting there is part of the experience. Walkers descend from Tansen on village trails through terraced farms and forest, a drop of nearly 900 m in about 2.5–3 hours. Others take a jeep on the road via the Brangdi valley, about 13 km and an hour. Either way, allow a half-day, and combine the visit with a riverside picnic.

highlights.title: The white palace façade
highlights.text: Columns, arched windows and a symmetrical white front rise straight from the rock above the river. Seen from the riverbank below, the palace stands out sharply against the green hills of the valley.

highlights.title: Story of Tej Kumari
highlights.text: The palace was built as a memorial to Khadga Shumsher's youngest wife, who died in 1892, and is said to honour her wish for a place of pilgrimage by the river. The romance and tragedy behind it draw many Nepali couples.

highlights.title: Restored rooms and museum
highlights.text: The 2017 restoration repaired the structure and added a museum with photographs, Rana-era objects and panels on the palace's history. Rooms are not lavishly furnished, but the high ceilings and verandas convey the scale of the original.

highlights.title: Kali Gandaki river
highlights.text: The Kali Gandaki, which rises near the Tibetan border and cuts through the Himalaya at Mustang, flows broad and green-grey below the palace. Sandbanks and boulders make good picnic spots in the dry season.

highlights.title: Trail down from Tansen
highlights.text: The walking route from Tansen passes Magar and Brahmin villages, terraced millet and maize fields and patches of forest. It is one of the most rewarding half-day hikes in Palpa, with the palace appearing suddenly at the bottom.

how_to_reach.text: From Tansen, village trails descend to the Kali Gandaki in about 2.5–3 hours, a drop of roughly 870 m over 8–9 km. The return climb takes 3.5–4 hours, so most walkers arrange a jeep back. A local guide is recommended, as trails branch through villages.

A jeep road runs from Tansen via the Brangdi river valley to near the palace, ≈ 13 km · 1 h, with a short walk at the end. The road is rough in places and can be closed by landslides in the monsoon. Occasional local buses run in the afternoon.

where_to_stay: There is no hotel at Ranighat; the palace is a day destination. Stay in Tansen, where Hotel Srinagar on the hill above town is the most comfortable choice and old-town guesthouses suit budget travellers. From Tansen you can walk down in the morning, picnic by the river and return by jeep in the afternoon. A few simple teashops near the palace sell drinks and noodles, but there are no guest rooms suitable for visitors.
tips: Walk down and jeep back; the 870 m climb back up to Tansen is hot and steep for most visitors.
Carry a packed lunch and at least 1.5 litres of water per person, as shops near the palace are few.
Start the walk by 8 am from October to April to avoid midday heat in the valley.
Check road conditions in the monsoon, when the Brangdi valley road can be cut by landslides.
Do not swim in the Kali Gandaki; currents are strong even when the surface looks calm.

experiences.title: Hike from Tansen down to Rani Mahal
experiences.price_hint: ≈ ₹4,500 per group for guide and jeep return
experiences.image_query: Tansen Rani Mahal trail Palpa village
experiences.summary: A half-day walk of about 9 km from Tansen down through villages and forest to the Kali Gandaki and Rani Mahal, descending nearly 900 m, with a riverside picnic and a jeep ride back up to town.
body: We leave Tansen at about 7.30 am and walk out of town past the last houses onto a stone and earth trail heading north-west. The path drops steadily through terraced fields of maize, millet and mustard, small Magar and Brahmin settlements and pockets of sal and chilaune forest. Villagers use the trail daily, and you will share it with goats, school children and porters.

After 2.5–3 hours the valley opens, and the white palace comes into view on its rock above the river. We visit the palace and museum, then picnic on the riverbank. The descent is about 870 m in total, so knees take most of the strain; walking poles help.

In the early afternoon a jeep collects us for the hour-long drive back up to Tansen along the Brangdi valley. Fit walkers can climb back on foot in 3.5–4 hours. The hike is graded easy to moderate and suits anyone used to walking downhill for a few hours.

faqs.q: How difficult is the walk from Tansen to Rani Mahal?
faqs.a: It is easy to moderate: about 9 km and 2.5–3 hours, almost all downhill with a drop of roughly 870 m. The main challenge is the strain on knees. Walking poles and good shoes help. Taking a jeep back avoids the steep climb up, which makes it suitable for most reasonably active travellers.

faqs.q: Do we need a guide for the Rani Mahal hike?
faqs.a: It is strongly recommended. Trails branch through villages, and signage is limited. A local guide keeps you on the right path, explains village life and the palace history, and arranges the jeep pick-up. Our Tansen packages include a guide for this walk.

faqs.q: Can children do the Rani Mahal hike?
faqs.a: Active children aged eight and above usually manage well, especially with the jeep return. The trail has some steep, uneven sections, so closed shoes are essential. Carry plenty of water and snacks, and start early to avoid midday heat in the valley.

experiences.title: Rani Mahal palace rooms and museum
experiences.summary: An hour inside the restored palace with a guide, covering the 1893 building, Khadga Shumsher Rana's rise and exile, Tej Kumari's story, and the photographs and objects displayed in the small museum since the 2017 restoration.
body: The palace was built over about four years with labour drawn from surrounding villages, and is said to have been designed by a British architect, with craftsmen brought from India. Its plan follows European models: a central block with verandas, high-ceilinged rooms and stairways, all in brick and lime plaster. Your guide points out the original details that survived a century of abandonment.

The museum rooms tell the story of Khadga Shumsher, a powerful member of the Rana family who served as governor in Palpa, and of his flight to India in 1902 amid Rana court rivalries, after which the palace fell into ruin. Panels and photographs show the building before and after restoration.

The visit takes about an hour. Rooms are simply furnished, so the experience is more about the building and its setting than about fine interiors. Step out onto the river-facing terraces for the best views of the Kali Gandaki. Opening hours and fees are set by the local municipality; check current status before you travel.

faqs.a: General Khadga Shumsher Jang Bahadur Rana, a member of Nepal's ruling Rana family who served in Palpa, built it in 1893 in memory of his youngest wife, Tej Kumari Devi, who died in 1892. He fled to India in 1902, and the palace was abandoned for decades.

faqs.q: Why is Rani Mahal called the Taj Mahal of Nepal?
faqs.a: Like the Taj Mahal in Agra, Rani Mahal was built by a grieving husband as a memorial to his wife and stands beside a river. The comparison is about its story and setting rather than its size or architecture, which is European neoclassical.

Since the 2017 restoration, the palace houses a small museum with photographs, panels on its history and Rana-era objects. Rooms are mostly unfurnished, with high ceilings and verandas. The building's setting above the Kali Gandaki is as much a draw as the interior.

experiences.title: Riverside picnic on the Kali Gandaki
experiences.price_hint: Packed lunch ≈ ₹600 per person from Tansen
experiences.summary: A relaxed packed lunch on the sandbanks and boulders below Rani Mahal, with the palace above, the Kali Gandaki flowing past and time to sit, photograph and paddle at the edge before heading back to Tansen.
body: The Kali Gandaki is one of Nepal's great rivers, rising near the Tibetan border and cutting through the Himalaya between Dhaulagiri and Annapurna before flowing south past Palpa. Below Rani Mahal, in the dry season, it leaves wide sandbanks and smooth boulders along the bank, ideal for a picnic.

We carry a packed lunch from Tansen, usually sandwiches, boiled eggs, fruit, local snacks and tea in flasks, and settle in a shaded spot with a view of the palace. It is a good time for photographs of the white façade reflected in calmer water, and for watching local boats or fishermen when they are about.

The water is cold and the current strong, so paddling should stay at the very edge. From June to September the river rises sharply and the sandbanks disappear, so we only offer the picnic from November to April. Please carry all litter back to Tansen.

faqs.q: Is it safe to swim in the Kali Gandaki at Ranighat?
faqs.a: No. Even in the dry season the Kali Gandaki has strong currents and cold water, and drowning accidents happen. Paddling at the very edge on calm sandbanks is the limit. In the monsoon the river is high and dangerous, and we do not go to the bank.

faqs.q: Can we buy food at Rani Mahal?
faqs.a: A few small teashops near the palace sell drinks, biscuits and instant noodles, but there is no restaurant. Bring a packed lunch from Tansen. Hotel Srinagar and old-town cafés can prepare picnic boxes with a day's notice.

faqs.q: When is the best season for a Ranighat picnic?
faqs.a: November to April, when the river is low and sandbanks are exposed. December to February is coolest and most pleasant, though mornings can be foggy in the valley. March and April are warmer and still dry, with spring flowers on the trail.

Rani Mahal, also called Ranighat Durbar or Ranighat Palace, is on the bank of the Kali Gandaki in Palpa district, north-west of Tansen. It is about 13 km from Tansen by road via the Brangdi valley, or 8–9 km on foot on village trails descending nearly 900 m.

faqs.q: How do I get to Rani Mahal from Tansen?
faqs.a: Walk down on village trails in 2.5–3 hours, or take a jeep along the Brangdi valley road in about an hour, followed by a short walk. Most visitors walk down and return by jeep. Occasional local buses run in the afternoon but are slow and crowded.

Rani Mahal was completed in 1893, after about four years of work. General Khadga Shumsher Rana built it in memory of his wife Tej Kumari, who died in 1892. It was abandoned after he fled to India in 1902 and restored by the government in 2017.

faqs.q: Is Rani Mahal open to visitors?
faqs.a: Yes. Since the 2017 restoration, the palace has been open with a small museum, managed by the local municipality. A modest entry fee is charged. Opening hours and fees can change, so check current status before you travel, especially on public holidays.

faqs.q: How long should I spend at Rani Mahal?
faqs.a: Plan a half-day from Tansen: 2.5–3 hours to walk down or an hour by jeep, about an hour at the palace and museum, a riverside picnic, and an hour's jeep ride back. Fit walkers who climb back on foot should allow a full day.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Rani Mahal?
faqs.a: October to April is best, with dry trails and low water. December to February is cool and pleasant for walking. The monsoon from June to September brings slippery trails, landslides on the road and a high, fast river, so visits are harder.

faqs.q: Is Rani Mahal suitable for elderly visitors?
faqs.a: Yes, if they go by jeep rather than on foot. The jeep road ends a short walk from the palace, and there are some steps and uneven ground. The steep village trail from Tansen is not recommended for anyone with knee problems.

faqs.q: What else can I combine with Rani Mahal?
faqs.a: Combine it with Tansen's old town walk, a Dhaka weaving workshop and the Srinagar hill sunrise for a two-night Tansen stay. On a longer trip, add Lumbini and the Buddhist sites to the south, or continue north to Pokhara on the Siddhartha Highway.

Khadga Shumsher Rana lost out in the power struggles within the Rana family and fled to India in 1902. With its owner in exile, the palace was left empty and slowly decayed for most of the 20th century, until government repairs and the 2017 restoration brought it back into use as a museum.
